question.leadin: The final holder of this title was Tokugawa Yoshinobu.
question.text: Prior to an 1868 restoration of imperial rule, what title was held by military rulers of Japan?
question.clue: A power vacuum created after the death of a holder of this title led to the Onin War, which initiated the Sengoku period.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about emperors of Japan.
swap.text: This man has the distinction of maintaining the longest reign of any Japanese emperor. He is more famously known for overseeing the Japanese surrender during World War II.
swap.clue: This ruler, who delivered the Jewel Voice Broadcast, later renounced his divinity in the Humanity Declaration.

question.leadin: This work depicts three fishing boats swept up in the title object near present-day Yokohama. --.
question.text: Name this Hokusai print depicting Mount Fuji in the background.
question.answerHtml: The <u>Great Wave off Kanagawa</u> (or <u>Kanagawa-oki</u> <u>nami</u> <u>ura</u>; or <u>Under the Wave off Kanagawa</u>)
question.clue: This woodblock print by Hokusai that depicts three fishing boats caught in the title phenomenon near the title location while traveling back towards Edo.

swap.leadin: The busiest one of these locations in the United States is Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International.
swap.text: Name these locations, such as O'Hare International. These locations often require extensive security checks before a traveller is allowed near a runway.
swap.clue: After several Montoneros and Peronists gathered at one of these places, right-wing snipers shot into the crowd during the Ezeiza massacre.

question.text: This document was created when Emperor Meiji took power in 1868. It laid out Meiji's goals for Westernization, and can be considered the first constitution of modern-day Japan.
question.clue: This document officially ceded power to Emperor Meiji whose third clause allowed the ability to pursue any occupation regardless of social standing.

swap.leadin: This man survived an assassination attempt by Lee Bong Chang, known as the Sakuradamon Incident.
swap.text: Name this emperor of Japan during World War II, who implored his people to "endure the unendurable" before surrendering.
swap.clue: This regent led a country during the Mukden Incident, which served as a pretext for his nation's invasion of Manchuria.

question.leadin: The first group to hold these titles was known as the shugo, and they included heads of the Hosokawa, Shiba, and Yamana clans.
question.text: Give this feudal title commonly awarded to regional lords in Japan. They typically governed individual provinces under the direction of the shogun.
question.clue: A new aristocratic class known as the kazoku, which worked on a system of hereditary peerage, replaced this noble class following the Meiji Restoration.

swap.leadin: During this period, emperors who retired to monasteries retained power in the system of cloistered rule.
swap.text: Name this period that succeeded the Nara Period. This period came to an end with the Genpei War.
swap.clue: Near this period's end, forces loyal to Emperor Sutoku lost a civil war called the Hogen Disturbance to his brother Go-Shirakawa.

question.leadin: He entered an alliance with Tokugawa Ieyasu in 1562 and promoted the work of Christian missionaries in order to weaken the influence of monks.
question.text: Name this man who overthrew the Ashikaga shogunate and unified half of Japan's provinces before committing suicide in 1582.
question.clue: This ruler constructed the fortress of Azuchi Castle, ordered the massacre of the warrior monks at Mount Hiei, and defeated Imagawa Yoshimoto at the Battle of Okehazuma.

swap.leadin: Identify the following historical periods of Japan.
swap.text: This period from 1193 to 1333 was begun by the ascension of Yoritomo to the shogunate.
swap.clue: The capital was moved from this city to Kyoto during the Kenmu Restoration.

question.text: This city near the Kyoto-Kobe-Osaka metropolis contains lots of tame deer that roam around its many temples. Todai-ji, 7 other temples, and a forest make up the UNESCO World Heritage site of this city.
question.clue: This was the first time when emperors adopted the title of "tenno," and other innovations during this period, such as the institution of a Council of State, were adopted in order to imitate the government at Changan and important Tang Chinese institutions.

swap.text: Yoritomi is considered the founder of this shogunate, which was succeeded by the Ashikaga.
swap.clue: Its puppet rulers attempted to revolt with the Jokyu war, but were crushed and remained silent for another century.

question.text: This ethnically Amis soldier was stationed on Morotai during the Japanese occupation of the Dutch East Indies and only surrendered when he was discovered in 1974.

swap.leadin: Name these dudes from Asian history who founded dynasties.
swap.text: After the Taira clan was defeated in the Battle of Dannoura, ending the Genpei War, this man became the first shogun of the Kamakura dynasty.
swap.clue: This man seduced the daughter of his warden after he was banished to Izu for twenty years when his father tried to remove Taira Kiyomori in the Heiji Disturbance.

question.leadin: Four brothers from this family established its "four houses"-the Northern, Southern, Ceremonial, and Capital-only to all die in the same year from smallpox.
question.text: Name this family that established a semi-hereditary claim on the positions of sessho and kampaku after the 8th century, allowing their patriarchs to exercise imperial authority by marrying their daughters to the emperor.
question.clue: This clan gained much power in the Heian period by marrying its daughters into the imperial family. Michinaga of this clan was the father-in-law of four emperors and grandfather to three.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Japanese naval battles.
swap.text: Taguchi Shigeyoshi's defection from the Taira helped Minamoto Yoshitsune lead his fleet to victory in this 1185 battle which effectively ended the Gempei War and cleared the way for founding of the Kamakura shogunate.
swap.clue: This battle saw Taguchi Shigeyoshi reveal the location of the Emperor's ship, and both the child-emperor Antoku and his grandmother, the widow of Kiyomori, committed suicide.

question.text: With the Asuka Period, the Kofun Period forms part of this period of Japanese history when the imperial capital was at Nara. This period shares its name with Japan's primary ethnic group and with the Japanese battleship that was the country's flagship for most of World War Two.

swap.leadin: Emperor Kotoku implemented this set of policies, which included the abolition of private landholding and a tax based on population instead of land use.
swap.text: Name this 645 A.D. set of centralizing reforms inspired by Tang Dynasty China, which brought Japan under the control of the imperial court.
swap.answerHtml: Taika Reforms [or Taika no Kaishin; or Great Reformation of the Taika Era]
swap.clue: This set of laws promulgated during the Asuka period, which curtailed the power of regional governors and imported traditions like the equal field system from China.

question.text: The story is often backdated to apply to the rule of this man, who became the first shogun of the Ashikaga shogunate after he'd originally allied with Go-Daigo whom he later turned against.
question.clue: The end of Hojo power came when this warlord overthrew Hojo Takatoki and established himself as shogun in 1336, thus beginning the Muromachi period, which was also known by his clan's name.

swap.text: Although it is an independent corporation, Sony is associated with Sumitomo Mitsui, one of these horizontally integrated conglomerates. These conglomerates took a leading role in the Japanese economy after the postwar dissolution of the zaibatsu.
